```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("_common.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(ape); library(ggtree); library(ggtreeExtra); library(ggnewscale) })
ed <- function(...) repo_path("Enrichments_metatranscriptomics", ...)
```

::: {.paper-links}
[Paper: Plominsky, Oliver *et al.* 2026, *mBio*](https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.03382-25)
[Code: Enrichments_metatranscriptomics](https://github.com/AaronAOliver/Enrichments_metatranscriptomics)
[Data: MAGs on Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18273293)
[SRA PRJNA1404287](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA1404287)
:::

Seaweed is hard to digest for two reasons. Its polysaccharides are diverse and
sulfated, and it contains polyphenols (phlorotannins and their breakdown
products) that inhibit microbial growth and enzymes. Hindgut contents from six
*Kyphosus cinerascens* fish were used to start anaerobic in vitro microcosms
fed different combinations of macroalgal and host-associated media. Four of
these kept 96 to 99% of the active hindgut families. They were sampled on days 3,
8 and 16 for paired metagenomics and metatranscriptomics.

Mapping RNA reads back to MAGs shows which genome expresses which enzyme, and
when. The early colonists detoxify polyphenols and degrade alginate. Later
guilds take on the more recalcitrant sulfated polysaccharides.

This notebook covers my part of the study: the genome-resolved expression
analysis and the figures built from it.

```{r load}
mag_info <- read.delim(ed("data", "microcosm_mag_info.txt"), check.names = FALSE) %>%
  filter(taxa != "Unclassified")
# one taxonomy per dereplicated population (bin_taxonomy.tab lists every member bin,
# and one population's members disagree, so it would double-count in a join)
parent_tax <- select(mag_info, parent_bin = bin, taxonomy = taxa)
map_rate <- read.delim(ed("data", "mapping_rate.tab"))

samples_ord <- c("FISH_1","FISH_2","FISH_3","FISH_4","FISH_5","FISH_6","T0_AVG",
                 "M30_T03","M30_T08","M30_T16","M36_T03","M36_T08","M36_T16",
                 "M75_T03","M75_T08","M75_T16","M78_T03","M78_T08","M78_T16")
sample_meta <- tibble(sample = samples_ord) %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(str_starts(sample, "FISH") ~ "Wild hindgut",
                           sample == "T0_AVG" ~ "Inoculum (T0)",
                           TRUE ~ str_extract(sample, "^M\\d+")),
         day = case_when(sample == "T0_AVG" ~ 0,
                         str_starts(sample, "M") ~ as.numeric(str_extract(sample, "\\d+$")),
                         TRUE ~ NA_real_))
tax_cols_mt <- tax_colors[c("Alphaproteobacteria","Bacillota","Bacteroidota","Candidatus Tefagiota",
                            "Desulfobacterota","Fusobacteriota","Gammaproteobacteria",
                            "Spirochaetota","Verrucomicrobiota")]
```

```{r summary-table}
tibble(
  Quantity = c("MAGs binned from fish, inoculum and microcosms", "Dereplicated populations used for read mapping",
               "Metatranscriptomes (6 fish, inoculum, 4 microcosms x 3 days)", "RNA reads that map to MAGs"),
  Value = c("1,153", "471", length(samples_ord),
            sprintf("%.0f to %.0f%%", min(map_rate$map_rate), max(map_rate$map_rate)))
) %>% knitr::kable(align = "lr")
```

## Approach

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  F[6 hindguts] --> I[Pooled inoculum] --> M[4 microcosms<br/>days 3, 8, 16]
  M --> G[Metagenomes<br/>1,153 MAGs<br/>dRep: 471 populations]
  M --> T[Metatranscriptomes<br/>Bowtie2 + RSEM]
  G --> A[dbCAN, SulfAtlas,<br/>CAMPER]
  A --> N[TPM per gene, scaled<br/>by mapping rate]
  T --> N
```

All samples (fish, inoculum and microcosms) were sequenced for both
metagenomes and metatranscriptomes.

Only `r sprintf("%.0f to %.0f%%", min(map_rate$map_rate), max(map_rate$map_rate))` of reads in each sample map to the binned genomes. Raw TPMs are
therefore scaled by each sample's mapping rate, so that expression is
comparable between samples with different binning coverage. This was the core
normalization step in the original analysis:

```{r normalization-code}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
# Scale RSEM TPMs by the fraction of reads that are MAG-resolved
rsem_norm <- rsem
for (samp in sample_list) {
  rate <- dplyr::filter(mapping_rate, sample == samp)$map_rate * 0.01
  rsem_norm[[samp]] <- rsem_norm[[samp]] * rate + 1e-8
}
# Collapse the four T0 replicates into a single inoculum profile
rsem_norm$T0_AVG <- rowMeans(rsem_norm[, c("T0_A", "T0_B", "T0_C", "T0_D")])
```

```{r mapping-rate}
#| fig-height: 3.2
map_rate %>%
  filter(sample %in% samples_ord | str_starts(sample, "T0")) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = unique(c(samples_ord[1:6], sort(sample[str_starts(sample, "T0")]),
                                                   samples_ord[8:19])))) %>%
  mutate(Group = case_when(str_starts(sample, "FISH") ~ "Wild hindgut",
                           str_starts(sample, "T0") ~ "Inoculum (T0 replicates)",
                           TRUE ~ "Microcosm"),
         Group = factor(Group, levels = c("Wild hindgut", "Inoculum (T0 replicates)", "Microcosm"))) %>%
  plot_ly(x = ~sample, y = ~map_rate, color = ~Group, type = "bar",
          colors = c("Wild hindgut" = "#4ea3ff", "Inoculum (T0 replicates)" = "#9aa3b2", Microcosm = site_teal),
          hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y:.1f}% of reads map to MAGs<extra></extra>") %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "", tickangle = -45), yaxis = list(title = "% of reads mapped to MAGs", ticksuffix = "%"),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = 1.15)) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

## The 471 populations

The tree shows the dereplicated MAG populations. The rings give each genome's
count of red-algal CAZymes, brown-algal CAZymes, sulfatases and
polyphenol-degrading genes. Bacteroidota and Verrucomicrobiota carry the most
sulfatases, about 20 per genome on average. Phloroglucinol and caffeate
degradation genes are spread more widely, and Gammaproteobacteria carry the
most per genome.

```{r tree}
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-cap: "Phylogeny of the 471 dereplicated MAG populations with gene-count rings."
env <- new.env()
suppressWarnings(load(ed(".RData"), envir = env))
tree <- env$tree
hl <- env$hilight_table %>% select(node = node_id, Taxonomy)

rings <- mag_info %>%
  transmute(bin,
            `Red algal CAZymes` = `red algal CAZy`, `Brown algal CAZymes` = `brown algal CAZy`,
            Sulfatases = sulfatase, `Polyphenol degradation` = `all phloroglucinol` + `caffeic acid degradation`) %>%
  pivot_longer(-bin, names_to = "Genes", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(Genes = factor(Genes, levels = c("Red algal CAZymes", "Brown algal CAZymes",
                                          "Sulfatases", "Polyphenol degradation")))

ggtree(tree, layout = "fan", open.angle = 10, colour = "grey75", linewidth = .2) +
  geom_highlight(data = hl, aes(node = node, fill = Taxonomy), alpha = .85, to.bottom = TRUE,
                 extendto = max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(tree)) * 1.02) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tax_colors, name = "MAG taxonomy", guide = guide_legend(ncol = 2, order = 1)) +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_fruit(data = rings, geom = geom_bar, stat = "identity", orientation = "y",
             mapping = aes(x = count, y = bin, fill = Genes), pwidth = .45, offset = .05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("indianred1", "#b38f3a", "gold", "#8cd2d5"), name = "Gene class",
                    guide = guide_legend(ncol = 2, order = 2)) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.key = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.text = element_text(colour = site_text, size = 11),
        legend.title = element_text(colour = site_text, size = 12, face = "bold"),
        legend.key.size = unit(.45, "cm"),
        legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical",
        plot.margin = margin(-0.6, 0, -0.6, -0.6, "in"))   # trim the empty margin ggtree leaves around a fan
```

### Enrichment in culture

Each point is a MAG population, placed by its relative abundance in the wild
hindgut (x) and its peak abundance in any microcosm sample (y). Points above the
diagonal were enriched by cultivation. Point size is the number of algal
CAZymes and sulfatases, and populations that were never detected are drawn at
10<sup>-6</sup>. Hover over a point to see its enzyme toolkit.

```{r enrichment-scatter}
#| fig-height: 5.5
mag_info %>%
  mutate(across(c(Natural, Microcosm), ~ pmax(.x, 1e-6)),
         label = paste0("<b>", bin, "</b><br>", taxa,
                        "<br>Red-algal CAZymes: ", `red algal CAZy`,
                        "<br>Brown-algal CAZymes: ", `brown algal CAZy`,
                        "<br>Sulfatases: ", sulfatase,
                        "<br>Phloroglucinol genes: ", `all phloroglucinol`,
                        "<br>Caffeate genes: ", `caffeic acid degradation`)) %>%
  plot_ly(x = ~Natural, y = ~Microcosm, color = ~taxa, colors = tax_cols_mt,
          size = ~ sulfatase + `brown algal CAZy` + `red algal CAZy` + 1, sizes = c(5, 30),
          type = "scatter", mode = "markers", text = ~label, hoverinfo = "text",
          marker = list(opacity = .75, line = list(width = .4, color = "#111"))) %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(type = "log", title = "Relative abundance in wild hindgut", exponentformat = "power"),
         yaxis = list(type = "log", title = "Peak relative abundance in microcosms", exponentformat = "power"),
         legend = list(itemsizing = "constant", title = list(text = "<b>Phylum</b>")),
         shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = 1e-6, y0 = 1e-6, x1 = 1, y1 = 1, xref = "x", yref = "y",
                            line = list(dash = "dot", color = "#888"))),
         annotations = list(list(x = -0.35, y = -0.85, xref = "x", yref = "y", text = "1:1",
                                 showarrow = FALSE, font = list(color = "#777", size = 11)))) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

The table lists the `r nrow(mag_info)` populations with a phylum assignment.

```{r mag-table}
mag_info %>%
  select(MAG = bin, Taxonomy = taxa, `Red algal CAZymes` = `red algal CAZy`,
         `Brown algal CAZymes` = `brown algal CAZy`, Sulfatases = sulfatase,
         `Phloroglucinol reductase` = `phloroglucinol reductase`,
         `Caffeate degradation` = `caffeic acid degradation`, Catalase = catalase,
         Dehalogenase = dehalogenase, `Wild hindgut` = Natural, `Microcosm max` = Microcosm) %>%
  nb_table(page = 8) %>%
  formatPercentage(c("Wild hindgut", "Microcosm max"), digits = 2)
```

## Expression of CAZymes and sulfatases over time

The plot below sums CAZyme and sulfatase TPM for each MAG population, grouped by
phylum, and follows each microcosm from the inoculum to day 16. Choose a
microcosm with the buttons.

```{r cazy-area}
#| fig-height: 5
cs <- read.csv(ed("parent_bin_cazy_sulf.csv"), check.names = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(-parent_bin, names_to = "sample", values_to = "tpm") %>%
  left_join(parent_tax, by = "parent_bin") %>%
  filter(!is.na(taxonomy), taxonomy != "Unclassified")

micro <- c("M30", "M36", "M75", "M78")
area <- map_dfr(micro, function(m) {
  cs %>% filter(sample == "T0_AVG" | str_starts(sample, m)) %>%
    mutate(microcosm = m, day = if_else(sample == "T0_AVG", 0, as.numeric(str_extract(sample, "\\d+$"))))
}) %>% group_by(microcosm, day, taxonomy) %>% summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = "drop")

taxa_present <- intersect(names(tax_cols_mt), unique(area$taxonomy))
fig <- plot_ly()
for (m in micro) for (tx in taxa_present) {
  d <- filter(area, microcosm == m, taxonomy == tx) %>% arrange(day)
  fig <- add_trace(fig, data = d, x = ~day, y = ~tpm, name = tx, type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
                   stackgroup = "one", line = list(width = .5, color = tax_cols_mt[[tx]]),
                   fillcolor = tax_cols_mt[[tx]], legendgroup = tx, showlegend = TRUE,
                   visible = m == micro[1],
                   hovertemplate = paste0(tx, "<br>day %{x}: %{y:,.0f} TPM<extra></extra>"))
}
nt <- length(taxa_present)
btns <- lapply(seq_along(micro), function(i)
  list(method = "update", label = micro[i],
       args = list(list(visible = rep(seq_along(micro) == i, each = nt)),
                   list(title = list(text = paste("Microcosm", micro[i]), font = list(size = 13), x = .99, xanchor = "right")))))
fig %>%
  layout(updatemenus = list(list(type = "buttons", direction = "right", buttons = btns,
                                 x = 0, y = 1.15, xanchor = "left", bgcolor = "#dfe5ec", bordercolor = "#8a93a3", font = list(color = "#111"))),
         title = list(text = "Microcosm M30", font = list(size = 13), x = .99, xanchor = "right"), margin = list(t = 70),
         xaxis = list(title = "Day", tickvals = c(0, 3, 8, 16), ticktext = c("T0", "3", "8", "16")),
         yaxis = list(title = "CAZyme + sulfatase TPM"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>Phylum</b>"))) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

### Share of each genome's transcription spent on these enzymes

For every MAG with at least 100 TPM in a sample, the plot shows the share of
its expression that goes to CAZymes, sulfatases or detoxification genes. At
their peak, individual Bacteroidota and Verrucomicrobiota MAGs put 5 to 7%
of their transcription into sulfatases. One Bacillota MAG puts over 20% into
detoxification genes.

```{r pct-expression}
#| fig-height: 5.5
pct <- bind_rows(
  read.delim(ed("cazy_expression_short.tab")) %>% mutate(set = "CAZymes"),
  read.delim(ed("sulf_expression_short.tab")) %>% mutate(set = "Sulfatases"),
  read.delim(ed("detox_expression_short.tab")) %>% mutate(set = "Detoxification")
) %>% filter(!is.na(taxonomy), taxonomy != "Unclassified") %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = samples_ord))

sets <- c("CAZymes", "Sulfatases", "Detoxification")
set.seed(2)
pct <- pct %>% mutate(xj = as.numeric(sample) + runif(n(), -.32, .32))
fig <- plot_ly()
for (s in sets) {
  fig <- add_trace(fig, data = filter(pct, set == s), x = ~xj, y = ~pct_relevant,
                   color = ~taxonomy, colors = tax_cols_mt, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
                   marker = list(size = 6, opacity = .75), visible = s == sets[1],
                   legendgroup = ~taxonomy, showlegend = TRUE,
                   text = ~paste0("<b>", parent_bin, "</b><br>", taxonomy, "<br>", sample,
                                  "<br>", round(100 * pct_relevant, 2), "% of MAG expression",
                                  "<br>MAG total: ", round(tpm_total), " TPM"),
                   hoverinfo = "text")
}
ntx <- n_distinct(pct$taxonomy)
btns <- lapply(seq_along(sets), function(i)
  list(method = "update", label = sets[i],
       args = list(list(visible = rep(seq_along(sets) == i, each = ntx)),
                   list(title = list(text = paste("Share of expression:", sets[i]), font = list(size = 13), x = .99, xanchor = "right")))))
fig %>%
  layout(updatemenus = list(list(type = "buttons", direction = "right", buttons = btns, x = 0, y = 1.15,
                                 xanchor = "left", bgcolor = "#dfe5ec", bordercolor = "#8a93a3", font = list(color = "#111"))),
         title = list(text = "Share of expression: CAZymes", font = list(size = 13), x = .99, xanchor = "right"), margin = list(t = 70),
         xaxis = list(title = "", tickvals = seq_along(samples_ord), tickangle = -60,
                      ticktext = replace(samples_ord, samples_ord == "T0_AVG", "Inoculum")),
         yaxis = list(title = "% of the MAG's expression", tickformat = ".0%"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>Phylum</b>")),
         shapes = lapply(c(6.5, 7.5, 10.5, 13.5, 16.5), function(x)
           list(type = "line", x0 = x, x1 = x, y0 = 0, y1 = 1, yref = "paper",
                line = list(color = "#bbb", width = 1)))) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

### Genomic potential vs. realized expression

The x-axis is the fraction of the genome that encodes each enzyme class. The
y-axis is the highest fraction of that MAG's transcripts in any sample. Points
near the dotted line express an enzyme class in proportion to its gene count.

```{r potential-vs-expression}
#| fig-height: 5
mp <- read.delim(ed("max_pct_1k.tab"), check.names = FALSE) %>% rename(taxonomy = `taxonomic group`) %>%
  filter(taxonomy != "Unclassified")
pairs <- list(CAZymes = c("pct_cazy_genome", "max_cazy_pct"),
              Sulfatases = c("pct_sulf_genome", "max_sulf_pct"),
              Detoxification = c("pct_detox_genome", "max_detox_pct"))
fig <- plot_ly()
for (s in names(pairs)) {
  d <- mp %>% transmute(bin, taxonomy, x = .data[[pairs[[s]][1]]], y = .data[[pairs[[s]][2]]]) %>%
    filter(!is.na(y))
  fig <- add_trace(fig, data = d, x = ~x, y = ~y, color = ~taxonomy, colors = tax_cols_mt,
                   type = "scatter", mode = "markers", visible = s == "CAZymes",
                   legendgroup = ~taxonomy, showlegend = TRUE,
                   marker = list(size = 8, opacity = .8, line = list(width = .4, color = "#111")),
                   text = ~paste0("<b>", bin, "</b><br>", taxonomy), hoverinfo = "text+x+y")
}
ntx <- n_distinct(mp$taxonomy)
# CAZymes span up to ~20%; sulfatases and detoxification stay under 5%, so zoom those panels to 0-5%
btns <- lapply(seq_along(pairs), function(i) {
  lay <- list(title = list(text = names(pairs)[i], font = list(size = 13), x = .99, xanchor = "right"))
  if (names(pairs)[i] == "CAZymes") {
    lay[["xaxis.autorange"]] <- TRUE; lay[["yaxis.autorange"]] <- TRUE
  } else {
    lay[["xaxis.range"]] <- c(0, .05); lay[["yaxis.range"]] <- c(0, .05)
  }
  list(method = "update", label = names(pairs)[i],
       args = list(list(visible = rep(seq_along(pairs) == i, each = ntx)), lay))
})
fig %>%
  layout(updatemenus = list(list(type = "buttons", direction = "right", buttons = btns, x = 0, y = 1.15,
                                 xanchor = "left", bgcolor = "#dfe5ec", bordercolor = "#8a93a3", font = list(color = "#111"))),
         title = list(text = "CAZymes", font = list(size = 13), x = .99, xanchor = "right"), margin = list(t = 70),
         xaxis = list(title = "Share of the genome's genes", tickformat = ".0%", rangemode = "tozero"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Highest share of the MAG's expression", tickformat = ".0%", rangemode = "tozero"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>Phylum</b>")),
         shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = 0, y0 = 0, x1 = .2, y1 = .2, line = list(dash = "dot", color = "#888")))) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

## Enzyme-level successions

Splitting expression by enzyme family shows the order of events. Alginate lyases
(PL6, PL7, PL17) and polyphenol pathways (phloroglucinol reductase, caffeate
reduction CarA to CarE, catalase) peak early, mostly in Gammaproteobacteria.
Carrageenan- and fucoidan-specific sulfatases and glycoside hydrolases rise
later. The panels below are the published versions of these figures.

::: {.panel-tabset}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Reproducing this page
The figures here use the processed summary tables in the
[repository](https://github.com/AaronAOliver/Enrichments_metatranscriptomics):
per-MAG expression shares, MAG metadata, and the dereplicated MAG
tree stored in `.RData`. The full RSEM gene-by-sample matrix
(`data/binned_expression_fixed.tab`), which `genome_resolved_expression.R`
reads, is not in the repository. The enzyme-level panels are therefore shown as
the published figures rather than recomputed here.
:::
